patterns.title: Aliased pointer args → raw-pointer args
patterns.why: Zig passes *Page, *Row and []Cell freely while integrity checks re-read the same page memory. In Rust a &mut argument is protected for the whole call, so re-reading that memory through another path is undefined behaviour. The port takes raw pointers, as Zig does, and only makes a short-lived &mut slice for the final fill.

patterns.title: Intrusive links and @fieldParentPtr → field-address trait and offset_of!
patterns.why: Zig's intrusive containers reach the element's next field by name at compile time, and recover a parent struct from a field pointer with @fieldParentPtr. Rust has neither generic field access nor a protector-free &mut, so a per-type trait hands out the field's address and the queue reads and writes links through raw pointers; the parent is recovered by subtracting offset_of! from the address, over exposed provenance.

patterns.title: comptime parameters → const generics + #[inline]
patterns.why: A comptime width lets Zig monomorphise the cell loop so each store is a fixed-size write. The first port took the width as a runtime enum, and every store became a dynamic-length copy (one memcpy call per cell). The fix gives the width as a const generic, dispatched once per row, which is the Rust form of Zig's inline-else switch.

patterns.title: packed struct(u64) → explicit shift-and-mask bitfield
patterns.why: Zig lays a terminal cell out as a packed struct(u64) and reads fields by name; @bitCast turns it into a u64 and back for free. Rust has no packed bitfields, so the cell is a #[repr(transparent)] u64 with shift constants, get_bits/set_bits helpers and one accessor pair per field. A layout test checks every shift against the reference.

patterns.title: Zig byte slices → &[u8] / Vec<u8>, never a lossy String
patterns.why: A Zig []const u8 is bytes, not validated UTF-8. A window title set by an escape sequence can hold invalid UTF-8, and the reference keeps those bytes as they are. The port keeps &[u8] / Vec<u8> and drops the NUL sentinel at the API edge. It copies with memmove (core::ptr::copy) because the caller may pass the title's own buffer back in.
